-----
Coram: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Gautam Kumar Choudhary
-----
 For the Petitioner : M/s Sahil & Saurabh Narayan, Advocates
 For the State : Mr. Nawin Kr. Singh, A.P.P.
 For O.P. No. 2 : M/s Baibhaw Gahlaut & Subhneet Jha, Advocates
 -----
 Oral Order
 14 / Dated : 13.06.2024

1 .  The instant criminal revision petition has been preferred against the judgment of conviction passed in Cr. Appeal No. 116/2019 by which the petitioner has been convicted and sentenced under Section 498A and 323 of Indian Penal Code and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year and three months respectively.
2. Learned counsel for the petitioner confines his argument on the point of sentence and submitted that the petitioner is the practicing lawyer at Arval District Court, Bihar.
There is no past conviction proved against him and he has absolutely no criminal antecedent.
One case under Section 494 of Indian Penal Code had been lodged by the complainant-wife in which the petitioner has been acquitted of the charge and his wife has already performed second marriage.
In the present case, he has already served 4 months of imprisonment.

3. Learned counsel for the State, assisted by learned counsel for opposite party no. 2, has defended the impugned order and submitted that the past conduct of the petitioner does not deserve him any leniency and after filing the revision he had absconded and did not appear before this Court.
Having considered the submission advanced on behalf of both sides, this Court is of the view that the period already undergone by the petitioner will serve the ends of justice.

The judgment of conviction is affirmed and that of sentence is modified to the extent of the period already undergone Santosh Kumar vs The State Of Jharkhand on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/186786787/
1 by the petitioner.
